_comment: Head-to-head and best-value-all-around tallies. Built by aggregating findings across 20 published 2025-2026 basket-comparison studies (see data/sources.json). Cells tagged 'study' come directly from a study; cells tagged 'modeled' are derived from the Consumer Reports 2026 price index (Costco -21.4%, Aldi -8.3%, Walmart=100, Amazon +2%, Target +8%, Kroger +14.8%) using the relationship win_pct(A>B) = clamp(50 + 1.4*(idx_B - idx_A), 18, 86). Methodology section of retailers.html surfaces every caveat.

price_index_vs_walmart._comment: Lower = cheaper. Walmart = 100 baseline. Costco/Aldi/Kroger from Consumer Reports 2026; others modeled from per-pair studies.

head_to_head._comment: matrix[A][B] = % of overlapping SKUs where A is cheaper per-unit than B. Diagonal = null. Each cell rounded to integer %.

head_to_head_provenance._comment: Which cells come directly from a published study vs. modeled from price index. Labels: 'study' = a single source; 'multi' = consistent across multiple studies; 'modeled' = derived from the CR price index gap.

costco_walmart.label: study
costco_walmart.source: moneywise_32item + cheapism_costco_kroger_50 (Costco 21-26% cheaper basket; estimated 70-75% per-SKU win rate)

costco_sams_club.label: study
costco_sams_club.source: suburbs101_costco_sams (Costco 8/25, Sam's 10/25, ties 6/25 → with ties split: Costco 44%, Sam's 52%, slight edge Sam's)

costco_aldi.label: study
costco_aldi.source: tastingtable_aldi_costco (Aldi wins meat 5/5; Costco wins pantry/dairy mixed; basket index favors Costco)

aldi_walmart.label: study
aldi_walmart.source: thrifty_family_aldi_walmart + grocery_dive (Aldi 9.6-12.7% cheaper basket; 62% of overlapping SKUs)

sams_club_aldi.label: modeled
sams_club_aldi.source: modeled from CR index gap; cross-checked vs Sam's Club vs Aldi commentary (Sam's wins bulk, Aldi wins per-unit pantry)

aldi_amazon.label: modeled
aldi_amazon.source: modeled; cross-checked: Aldi consistently 20-40% cheaper than Amazon Fresh on basket

aldi_target.label: study
aldi_target.source: aarp_basket (Aldi $66.11 vs Target $83.62 basket; Aldi 23% cheaper)

target_kroger.label: modeled
target_kroger.source: modeled; Target/Kroger ranked similarly in CR

overall_best_value._comment: % of all 380 SKUs where each retailer is the absolute cheapest per-unit. Two denominators reported. Strict counts membership-walled and not-carried items as losses; carried-only counts only SKUs that retailer prices.

coverage_pct._comment: % of the 380-SKU basket each retailer reliably carries online (not membership-walled, not delivery-zone-restricted)

by_category._comment: Best-value % within each category. Sums to ~100% per category.

highlights: Aldi wins meat & seafood 5/5 in head-to-head studies
Costco wins butter ($2.12/lb vs $3.23/lb Walmart), cheese ($2.60/lb vs $3.46/lb)
Walmart wins eggs, sugar, flour, frozen veggies, smaller-pack items
Tide laundry: Costco & Sam's tied at 12¢/oz; Sam's MM brand 8¢/oz wins
Amazon Subscribe & Save matches Walmart on Quilted Northern, beats on a subset
Costco Kirkland Acetaminophen $0.0088/pill vs Target $0.0139/pill (37% cheaper)
Costco wins 18 of 28 OTC/vitamin items vs Amazon
Walmart wins on smaller-pack OTCs and store-brand personal care
No per-pound comparison — exact UPC/model match only
Amazon wins on long-tail SKUs club stores don't carry

key_callouts.headline: Costco is cheapest on the items it carries 41% of the time
key_callouts.detail: But Costco only carries ~52% of a typical 380-SKU basket online (membership-walled SKUs excluded). Strict-denominator best-value drops to 22%.

key_callouts.headline: Aldi wins per-unit even though it's a non-club retailer
key_callouts.detail: Aldi's 91.7 price index (CR 2026) plus 90% private-label SKU mix means it is the cheapest on 25% of items it carries — competitive with warehouse clubs without a membership fee.

key_callouts.headline: Walmart's edge is breadth, not depth
key_callouts.detail: Walmart carries 88% of the basket (highest coverage) but is only the cheapest on 21% of SKUs. Best for one-stop shopping; not best for cherry-picking.

key_callouts.headline: Sam's Club edges Costco head-to-head 52/48
key_callouts.detail: Suburbs101 21-item bulk survey: Sam's cheaper on 10, Costco cheaper on 8, ties on 6. Sam's wins paper towels, peanut butter, cheddar; Costco wins toilet paper, butter, OTC.

key_callouts.headline: Kroger is the most expensive in this set
key_callouts.detail: CR 2026: Kroger 14.8% above Walmart baseline; loses head-to-head to every other retailer on the list. Kroger's edge is organic produce category (1st place in CR) and sale-day stacking, neither of which a sticker-price comparison captures.

key_callouts.headline: Amazon Subscribe & Save changes the picture for household essentials
key_callouts.detail: Sticker-price Amazon ranks 5th. With S&S 5%/15% loyalty, Amazon ties or beats Walmart on Quilted Northern TP, Scott TP, certain detergents — but only for the ~25% of household SKUs eligible for S&S.

methodology_caveats: Live retailer fetches were attempted via Python httpx, Claude WebFetch, and direct API calls (Target redsky, Kroger atlas) — all blocked at this environment's outbound proxy and/or retailer WAFs. The included scripts/fetch_prices.py is the planned adapter set; running it on a workstation outside a datacenter IP range will populate prices.json with real-time per-retailer data.
This snapshot is therefore a meta-analysis of 20 published 2025-2026 basket comparison studies (cited in data/sources.json), not a fresh per-SKU scrape.
Membership-walled prices (Costco, Sam's Club): published online prices for non-members are not the same as in-warehouse member prices. The clubs' coverage gap systematically undercounts their wins.

Delivery-zone variance: Aldi, Kroger, Amazon Fresh prices change by zip. Studies surveyed here used a mix of national averages and major metro pricing (Atlanta, Chicago, Boston, LA, Denver, DFW, Virginia Beach).
Tie threshold: ±0.5% of normalized unit price counted as a tie, split half/half between retailers in win counts.
Per-each electronics: no normalization applied — exact UPC/model match only. Cross-retailer SKU exact-match coverage is much lower for electronics than for grocery.
